summary: Validate shared readiness operation receipts and continue deterministically when an operation key is occupied by a different record.

replay.detail: Receipt validation uses the existing operation-ID index with a plain bounded read, no receipt ranking or full-history sort, and searches existing deterministic continuations before writing a new receipt. Each read retains at most 16 occupants with explicit overflow detection; one shared 64-visit allowance bounds reads and validations across branches. Overflow without a matching receipt in the window or exhausted work remains visibly pending, never vacant. Conflict diagnostics and logs are deduplicated across replay and restart; no additional journal state is needed.

schema.detail: No database schema change, new index or startup migration.

rules.detail: Shared readiness failure, notice and recovery receipts must match their expected daemon operation. Conflicts are recorded and logged; exhausted continuations remain pending without preventing other drain items from progressing. Blocked phase lookup never proves absence: recovery remains incomplete and retains the case until all phase occupancy can be resolved.

compatibility.detail: Shared readiness routing remains disabled by default. Normal operation keys and legacy weekly checkpoint bytes are unchanged.

manual.detail: Before disabling an enabled shared readiness sender, drain its active case and pending primary notices. Resolve any blocked operation conflicts first; receiver-side generic suppression remains independent of the sender option.

recovery.detail: Retain the existing journal across restart. If shared routing was disabled before draining, restore the same sender policy and journal to finish its pending work.
